claims.text: ALD performed on tungsten surfaces before copper infiltration produces an ultra-thin tungsten carbide interlayer.
The resulting tungsten carbide interlayer is uniform and nanometer-scale at the W–Cu interface.
A tungsten carbide interlayer enhances phonon coupling between tungsten and copper.
Enhanced phonon coupling reduces interfacial thermal resistance in the W–Cu composite.
Reducing W–Cu interfacial thermal resistance increases the composite's thermal conductivity.
The tungsten carbide interlayer is chemically stable under the proposed extreme operating conditions.
The tungsten carbide interlayer is mechanically stable under the proposed extreme operating conditions.
The chemical and mechanical stability of the interlayer preserves the composite's mechanical durability.
The chemical and mechanical stability of the interlayer preserves the composite's irradiation resistance.
The ALD-treated W–Cu composite will have significantly higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable untreated W–Cu composite.
The ALD-treated composite will suffer no loss of mechanical robustness relative to the untreated composite.
The ALD-treated composite will suffer no loss of irradiation resistance relative to the untreated composite.
The predicted benefits apply under high thermal flux and irradiation conditions representative of fusion-reactor joints.
Achieving the predicted benefits depends on the tungsten carbide layer being uniform and appropriately thin.
Deviations from the appropriate coating thickness or uniformity can eliminate the benefits or degrade thermal, mechanical, or irradiation-related performance.
